data.long_meaning: The Old English name Darrel is derived from two Old English words: ‘dæor’ meaning ‘deer’ and ‘rel’ meaning ‘counsel’ or ‘advice’. Darrel is a name of noble origin, suggesting a free man, a man of counsel, or a man of the deer. It was common among the Anglo-Saxons and the Normans. The name Darrel carries the meaning “Freeman, noble one” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Darrel usually hope their child will grow to embody freeman, noble one and live with faith, good character and purpose.
